record.title: A paper reports explanation-free shortcuts in automated interpretability evaluations
record.summary: An arXiv paper reports that construction cues in several automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines can predict stored scores without reading feature explanations. On rebuilt marks for 500 GPT-2 small features, the authors report a centre-mark rule at 0.979 balanced accuracy versus 0.838 for stored scorers, and a mark-count rule at 0.969. Their separate preregistered ranking test did not show that the tested simulation cue reordered features; an explanation-sensitive scorer exceeded explanation-free baselines on random-offset natural windows. These are bounded author-reported results, not evidence that automated interpretability as a field is invalid.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: arXiv lists version 1 of the paper as submitted on October 10, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On rebuilt marks for Neuronpedia stored fuzzing runs across 500 random GPT-2 small features, the author reports that 91.3% of activating examples place the peak on the centre token; a centre-mark rule reaches balanced accuracy 0.979 versus 0.838 for stored scorers, and a mark-count rule reaches 0.969. The marks were rebuilt from a scorer fork whose version is inferred.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that its tested simulation cue did not demonstrate feature reordering in a preregistered comparison; its 4-level rank-correlation result favors GPT-4, while the 10-level comparison does not separate the scorers. On random-offset natural-text windows over 49 features, the author reports that Jev with the actual explanation reaches pooled correlation 0.331 versus 0.013 with shuffled explanations and 0.015 for the best shared fixed-offset prior.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed paper does not establish independent reproduction, that the reported cues cause broad feature-ranking changes, or that the findings transfer beyond the sampled models, scorers, pipeline versions and protocols.

evidence_gaps.description: No code, archived raw examples, or data snapshot was inspected; some stored token marks are rebuilt from a fork whose exact version is inferred.
No independent group reproduced the baseline scores or assessed whether matched-item controls change the paper’s interpretation.
Transfer across other model families, scorer configurations and pipeline versions is unknown; the paper reports the centre cue was absent in a sampled set of 12 Gemma features.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, explanation-free shortcuts in named automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines would change local evaluation design and the interpretation of scorer comparisons across a meaningful research area. The evidence does not show broad ranking harm or invalidate the field.
limitations: Headline fuzzing baselines are calculated on marks rebuilt from a fork with inferred version; the author notes that displayed scores differ for 112 of 1,001 runs.

The paper reports no demonstrated feature-ranking change from the tested simulation cue. Its 4-level preregistered rank-correlation result favors GPT-4, while the 10-level comparison does not separate the scorers.
The natural-window control covers 49 features and changes the item construction; it does not by itself establish transfer to other models, scorers or evaluation pipelines.
No independent reproduction, code/data replay or preregistration artifact inspection was performed in this review.
brief.summary: An arXiv paper reports that construction cues in several automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines can predict stored scores without reading feature explanations. On rebuilt marks for 500 GPT-2 small features, the authors report a centre-mark rule at 0.979 balanced accuracy versus 0.838 for stored scorers, and a mark-count rule at 0.969. Their separate preregistered ranking test did not show that the tested simulation cue reordered features; an explanation-sensitive scorer exceeded explanation-free baselines on random-offset natural windows. These are bounded author-reported results, not evidence that automated interpretability as a field is invalid.

technical.claimed_result: The author reports strong explanation-free baselines on selected automated-interpretability evaluation data and a natural-window control where explanation-sensitive scores exceed shuffled-explanation and shared-position baselines; the tested simulation cue did not show feature reordering.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary arXiv v1 paper and its October 10 submission date are accessible and were read. Reported computed outcomes remain author claims; no independent code execution or reproduction was performed.
technical.mechanism: The paper attributes apparent prediction performance to item-construction cues, including peak-centred crops, fixed mark placement/counts in fuzzing items, and ordering of top-activating sequences. It proposes same-item comparison against the strongest explanation-free rule to test whether a score contains information about the explanation.
technical.regime: Author analyses cover Neuronpedia stored fuzzing runs for 500 random GPT-2 small features, current delphi and full-context fuzzing surfaces, OpenAI simulation sequences, and a random-offset natural-window test over 49 features. The paper also reports a 12-feature Gemma follow-up in which the position cue was absent.
technical.reproducibility: The article identifies public pipelines and describes its procedures, but no code, raw data or preregistration artifact was replayed in this review. The stored marks were reconstructed from a fork version the paper says is inferred.
technical.strongest_baseline: For rebuilt Neuronpedia marks, a centre-mark rule is reported at balanced accuracy 0.979 versus 0.838 for stored scorers; the mark-count rule reaches 0.969. For natural windows, the reported shared fixed-offset prior is 0.015, versus 0.331 for Jev with the real explanation and 0.013 with a shuffled explanation.

brief.title: A paper reports explanation-free shortcuts in automated interpretability evaluations
brief.why_it_matters: If these pipeline-specific shortcuts replicate, evaluation scores may partly reflect how examples and marks are constructed rather than the feature explanation itself. This affects how researchers compare automated-interpretability scorers and motivates same-item explanation-free controls. The paper’s mixed and adverse ranking results constrain the conclusion; it does not establish broad ranking harm or invalidate the field.
